title: One UI 9.5 Unveils X Game‑Changing Features for Samsung Phones – Android Police Reveals All
body:
Samsung has begun rolling out the first beta of One UI 9.5 to the newly launched Galaxy S26, bringing a suite of refinements that aim to tighten security, streamline multitasking and freshen the visual language across the flagship line‑up. Early testers report that the update feels like a substantial step forward, with native app‑locking, an overhauled Quick Settings panel, and a host of subtle performance tweaks that collectively make the S26 feel “new again.” The beta, currently limited to select markets, is expected to expand globally in the coming weeks as Samsung gathers feedback before the final release later this year.

One of the most noticeable additions is a built‑in app lock that eliminates the need for third‑party solutions. Users can now protect individual apps with a fingerprint, face scan, or PIN directly from the Settings menu, a feature that previously required Samsung’s Knox security suite or external apps. This move underscores Samsung’s push toward tighter integration of privacy tools within the core OS, aligning the company with broader industry trends that prioritize on‑device data protection without compromising convenience.

Multitasking also receives a boost. The new One UI 9.5 introduces a “Smart Switch” gesture that lets users flick a corner of the screen to pull up a floating window of a recently used app, facilitating quick reference without leaving the current task. Coupled with an upgraded split‑screen mode that now supports drag‑and‑drop of apps into the dual‑pane layout, the update aims to make productivity on a smartphone feel more akin to a desktop experience. For power users who rely on the S Pen, the beta adds a contextual menu that surfaces relevant shortcuts based on the active app, reducing the steps needed to launch note‑taking or annotation tools.

Visually, Samsung has refined the aesthetic of One UI with a softer color palette and refreshed iconography that leans toward a more minimalist design. The Quick Settings panel now groups related toggles under collapsible headings, decluttering the interface and making it easier to locate seldom‑used controls. Additionally, a new “Dynamic Wallpaper” option syncs the home screen background with the time of day, subtly shifting hues to match ambient lighting—a small but appreciated touch that enhances the overall user experience.

Performance-wise, Samsung claims the beta delivers up to a 10 percent improvement in app launch times and a modest reduction in battery drain, thanks to optimizations in the underlying Android 14 framework and tighter integration with the Exynos 2400 chipset. Early impressions from testers corroborate these claims, noting smoother transitions and a more responsive feel when navigating between apps. While the improvements are incremental rather than revolutionary, they demonstrate Samsung’s commitment to polishing the software experience throughout the device’s lifecycle, not just at launch.

Looking ahead, the One UI 9.5 beta serves as a testing ground for features that could roll out to older Samsung devices, extending the lifespan of the brand’s extensive portfolio. As the company prepares for the final public release, user feedback will likely shape the final feature set, potentially influencing the roadmap for upcoming models such as the Galaxy S27 and future foldables. If the beta’s enhancements are any indication, Samsung appears poised to reinforce its position as a leader in Android customization, delivering a more secure, efficient and visually cohesive ecosystem for its global user base.
